tasks.title: Document how to extend the autonomy backlog
tasks.summary: When the autonomy task queue is empty and `autonomy-seed-next` reports backlog exhaustion, operators need a clear, validated path to add the next alpha-critical task template. Document the rules and tighten the failure message so the loop doesn't stall.
expectedFailureModes: Autonomy sessions stall because there is no documented way to add the next backlog template safely.
New backlog entries break validation because required fields or workflow enums are missing.
Contributors add task templates that include local-only identifiers or unvalidated commands, making the public record brittle.
tasks.nextAction: Document how to add a new task template to agent-os/autonomy/backlog.json (fields, enums, verification), and update the backlog exhaustion error to point at that process.

tasks.title: Add CLI to scaffold new backlog templates
tasks.summary: Manual editing works, but backlog templates are still easy to get wrong. Add a small CLI that appends a minimal, validator-friendly template skeleton (with safe defaults) and forces the author to fill in the parts that matter before seeding.
expectedFailureModes: Backlog templates are added with missing required fields or invalid enum values, forcing repeated fixups.
Template IDs collide with existing task files, causing `autonomy-seed-next` to remain exhausted.
Verification commands drift into machine-local paths or secrets because there is no scaffold guidance.
tasks.nextAction: Create a script that appends a new backlog template skeleton with a validated `id`, default `state=proposed`, safe empty lists, and a reminder checklist, then update docs to point to it.

tasks.title: Write alpha release evidence runbook
tasks.summary: Alpha releases need a repeatable runbook that explains what evidence is generated, where it lands, and how to validate it. Document the end-to-end flow using the existing alpha release evidence script without implying public signing or publication policy.
expectedFailureModes: Release evidence exists but operators cannot reproduce it without reverse-engineering scripts.
Docs overclaim public verifiability or signing before key custody and publication are decided.
Evidence artifacts are generated but not checked into the release bundle, leaving the release unverifiable later.
humanEscalation: Human decision remains required for any public signing keys, key rotation, and release publication.
tasks.nextAction: Document the alpha release evidence workflow: prerequisites, commands, output locations, and how to interpret evidence, leaving signing/publishing as explicitly human-owned.

tasks.title: Document live CLI build prerequisites
tasks.summary: Make the live-test documentation explicit that cross-crate CLI live tests execute target/debug/covenant and therefore require cargo build -p covenant before targeted live runs.
expectedFailureModes: A targeted live CLI test uses a stale target/debug/covenant binary.
Operators run the documented command and get a misleading unknown-command failure.
The full quick gate passes while an isolated live CLI command fails because the binary prerequisite is implicit.
tasks.nextAction: Document the cargo build -p covenant prerequisite for targeted live CLI tests and update public live coverage docs.

tasks.title: Define capability scope schemas
tasks.summary: Specify stable scope payload shapes for each capability action namespace before enforcing more granular signed permissions in code.
expectedFailureModes: Capability scopes remain arbitrary JSON with no compatibility contract.
Future code enforcement rejects existing grants because no schema migration path exists.
Public docs imply scoped permissions are stronger than the current implementation can prove.
tasks.nextAction: Write the capability scope schema contract and mark any enforcement gaps explicitly.

tasks.title: Define audit root signing policy
tasks.summary: Record the first public policy for signing audit roots and publishing verifiable provenance without overclaiming immutable transparency.
expectedFailureModes: Audit integrity remains local-only while docs imply public verifiability.
Signing identity, key rotation, and root subject formats are left ambiguous.
Release artifacts cannot tie audit roots to task and commit provenance.
tasks.nextAction: Add an architecture decision record for audit root signing and update status/docs to match.

tasks.title: Document repeatable Linux gVisor runner setup
tasks.summary: Document the repeatable Linux host prerequisites for the opt-in runsc/rootfs live sandbox test before making stronger sandbox claims.
expectedFailureModes: The gVisor live test exists but cannot be reproduced by contributors.
Sandbox status claims outpace the tested Linux environment.
Rootfs, runsc, and environment variable prerequisites are scattered across test code.
tasks.nextAction: Write the repeatable Linux gVisor live-test runner guide and link it from runtime sandbox docs.

tasks.title: Let autonomy-next seed a backlog task
tasks.summary: When every tracked task is integrated or blocked, let autonomy-next optionally seed the next backlog template so autonomous runs can continue without a separate continuation pass.
expectedFailureModes: Automation dead-ends on autonomy-next even though a backlog template exists.
Seeding produces an invalid task JSON record or bypasses autonomy validation.
Seed mode mutates the task directory without leaving durable evidence in events.
tasks.nextAction: Add a seed option to autonomy-next, document it, and ensure it keeps autonomy state consistent when invoked in a clean worktree.

tasks.title: Add actor metadata when seeding tasks
tasks.summary: Allow autonomy-seed-next to record which role seeded a task and why, so events.jsonl can be audited without guessing the actor or intent.
expectedFailureModes: Seed events all look identical, obscuring whether they were seeded by a planner or an automation loop.
Invalid role strings are accepted and break autonomy validation later.
Notes capture machine-local identifiers that should never land in public history.
tasks.nextAction: Teach autonomy-seed-next to accept --actor and --note flags and apply them to the recorded seed event.

tasks.title: Implement audit root signature generation
tasks.summary: Add deterministic signing and verification for audit-root-attestation.v1 payloads so provenance claims can be verified end-to-end without overclaiming public transparency.
expectedFailureModes: Signatures are generated but the signature metadata format is underspecified and breaks across versions.
Verification accepts malformed payloads or incorrect subjects, undermining the trust boundary.
Docs overclaim public verifiability when keys are still local-only and not rotated.
tasks.nextAction: Choose the signing identity and key format, implement signing + verification, and record the security review notes before integration.

tasks.title: Validate capability scopes at grant time
tasks.summary: Validate versioned capability scope payloads when creating grants so enforcement can be strict without breaking existing callers or accepting arbitrary JSON.
expectedFailureModes: Invalid scope payloads are accepted and later cause enforcement-time failures.
A stricter validator rejects existing persisted grants without a migration path.
Docs imply scoped permissions are enforced even when validation is still permissive.
tasks.nextAction: Define the minimal accepted schema per capability, validate on grant creation, and track any compatibility gaps explicitly.

tasks.title: Add JSON output to peers list

expectedFailureModes: Live tests parse `peers list` output and extract the wrong token prefix or pubkey when rendering changes.
`--json` output omits `truncated` context, causing operators to assume the result set is exhaustive.
JSON output accidentally leaks token bytes, private key material, or other redacted peer registry fields.
tasks.nextAction: Implement `covenant peers list --json`, update the live tests that currently parse human output, and document the machine output contract.

expectedFailureModes: Automation scripts scrape stderr and misclassify ambiguous matches as success.
`--json` output changes exit codes or mixes human + JSON output, breaking parsers.
JSON output includes full token bytes or other redacted registry data.
tasks.nextAction: Implement `covenant peers revoke --json` with a stable outcome schema and keep human output unchanged by default.

expectedFailureModes: The JSON schema drifts without notice, breaking scripts that rely on it.
The CLI prints JSON to stdout but also emits human hints, producing invalid JSON.
`truncated` is incorrect when the daemon returns fewer rows than the limit but still had more peers available.
tasks.nextAction: Add live coverage for `--json` output and update the coverage matrix to point at the new test file.

tasks.title: Cover peers revoke JSON output in live tests

expectedFailureModes: JSON mode prints human hints to stderr, breaking automation that expects clean JSON output.
Ambiguous-match JSON leaks more peer registry data than the human output (token bytes, full tokens, or local paths).
Exit codes diverge between human and JSON modes, causing scripts to misclassify failures as success.
tasks.nextAction: Add the live JSON revoke test and update the coverage matrix/docs to reference it.

tasks.title: Enforce peer capability scope predicates

expectedFailureModes: A scoped `peers.revoke` grant can revoke a different peer than the signed selector.
A scoped `peers.list` grant can enumerate peers outside the signed scope, leaking metadata.
Docs imply scoped peer permissions are enforced when dispatch still treats peer scope fields as compatibility metadata.
tasks.nextAction: Write the peer scope predicate contract, implement enforcement in covenantd, and add focused tests for scope mismatch rejections.

tasks.title: Enforce settlement capability scope predicates
tasks.summary: Define and enforce stable settlement scope predicates so receipt reads and batch operations are constrained by signed scope metadata before expanding on-chain claims.
expectedFailureModes: Settlement grants remain effectively unscoped and allow arbitrary receipt reads or batch creation.
Future enforcement rejects existing grants because no explicit schema or migration path exists.
Public docs overclaim settlement isolation before dispatch-time predicates exist.
tasks.nextAction: Write settlement scope schema, implement dispatch checks for receipt reads and batch operations, and add tests that assert scope mismatches are rejected.

tasks.title: Add protocol info compatibility fixtures

tasks.nextAction: Triaged task: extend live_cli_verify_json to induce drift and assert verify --json exits non-zero with actionable drift repair fields.

tasks.title: Add bounded A2A background retry scheduler
tasks.summary: Turn the explicit stale-lease retry scan into an opt-in periodic scheduler after receiver-side idempotency caching exists.
expectedFailureModes: Background retry repeats externally visible side effects because receiver-side dedupe is absent or bypassed.
Retry scheduling creates unbounded queue churn when a recipient is down or a task is permanently invalid.
Operators cannot see why a retry was attempted, skipped, exhausted, or stopped.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd a2a --locked
humanEscalation: Human approval is required before enabling any background retry scheduler by default.
tasks.nextAction: Implement an opt-in periodic scheduler that reuses the existing retry gate, enforces backoff and exhaustion limits, and records audit-visible retry decisions.

tasks.title: Add alpha release bundle scaffold
tasks.summary: The alpha release contract defines evidence bundles, but operators still have to create the directory and notes by hand. Add a small non-publishing scaffold command that creates a release evidence bundle with generated evidence, a validation notes template, and a dry-run path.
expectedFailureModes: Operators generate evidence JSON but forget validation notes or release decisions.
Release bundle ids include unsafe path traversal or machine-local names.
The scaffold overwrites prior release evidence without an explicit operator decision.
tasks.nextAction: Create an alpha release bundle scaffold command, update release docs and landing docs to point at it, and verify the dry-run path.

tasks.title: Add alpha release bundle validator
tasks.summary: Release bundles can now be scaffolded, but there is no mechanical check that the bundle contains parseable evidence, validation notes, and a recorded decision. Add a small validator so alpha release evidence can fail closed before publication decisions.
expectedFailureModes: A bundle is missing evidence.json or validation.md but still treated as release evidence.
Evidence JSON is malformed or from the wrong schema kind.
A bundle with dirty evidence, pending gates, or no decision is accepted silently.
tasks.nextAction: Add a release bundle validator command, document it in the alpha release runbook, and verify help plus a generated self-test bundle.

tasks.title: Add alpha release readiness report
tasks.summary: Alpha evidence bundles can be generated and validated, but there is no single local command that summarizes the repository-level blockers before a human release decision. Add a read-only readiness report that checks dirty state, identity guards, README/status drift, autonomy records, provenance, live coverage metadata, and GitHub push attribution.
expectedFailureModes: Release operators miss a known blocker because release evidence commands are scattered across docs.
The readiness command mutates state or attempts a push while checking release prerequisites.
A read-only GitHub push attribution failure is hidden instead of surfaced as a release blocker.
tasks.nextAction: Add a read-only alpha release readiness command with text and JSON output, document it in release validation docs and landing docs, and keep push attribution as a reported blocker rather than a mutating step.

tasks.title: Add Git metadata write preflight
tasks.summary: Autonomous runs can currently implement and validate a slice before discovering that the local environment cannot write .git/index.lock for staging or commits. Add a read-only-safe preflight that detects whether Git metadata is writable and expose it through alpha readiness reporting.
expectedFailureModes: Autonomous runs only discover a read-only Git index after implementation and validation work is complete.
The preflight mutates repository history or leaves files behind in .git.
Alpha readiness hides the Git write-access blocker and implies commits can be made when they cannot.
tasks.nextAction: Add a Git metadata write-access validator, wire it into alpha readiness output, document the blocker semantics, and validate the help/readiness paths.

tasks.title: Add autonomy environment preflight
tasks.summary: Autonomous runs can now report alpha readiness blockers, but the autonomy loop itself still lacks a focused preflight that tells an agent whether local identity, Git metadata write access, and push attribution are usable before starting a slice. Add a read-only preflight report for autonomous sessions.
expectedFailureModes: Autonomous sessions start implementation despite an environment that cannot stage or commit.
The preflight hides GitHub push attribution blockers and encourages unsafe remote writes.
The preflight leaks machine-local paths in machine-readable output.
tasks.nextAction: Add an autonomy preflight command with text and JSON output, include Git write-access and identity blockers, document it in the autonomous workflow, and validate the expected local blocker path.

tasks.title: Add autonomy dirty handoff report
tasks.summary: When Git metadata is read-only, autonomous work can be validated but not committed. Add a read-only handoff report that summarizes dirty files, diff stats, task state, and preflight blockers so another environment can resume without reverse-engineering the working tree.
expectedFailureModes: A blocked autonomous session leaves uncommitted work with no machine-readable handoff.
The report leaks machine-local paths or private identity metadata.
The report tries to stage, commit, push, or mutate Git metadata while documenting a dirty tree.
tasks.nextAction: Add an autonomy dirty-report command with text and JSON output, document it in autonomous workflow docs, and validate it against the current dirty tree.

tasks.title: Add autonomy handoff bundle export
tasks.summary: Dirty reports summarize blocked work, but they do not contain enough content to reconstruct untracked files in another environment. Add a read-only handoff bundle command that emits the tracked patch, untracked text file contents, dirty report, and restore guidance without staging, committing, pushing, or writing Git metadata.
expectedFailureModes: A dirty handoff lists untracked files but omits their contents, making recovery incomplete.
The bundle leaks machine-local paths or private identity strings.
The bundle command mutates Git metadata while attempting to export blocked work.
tasks.nextAction: Add an autonomy handoff bundle command with JSON output, document it in autonomous workflow docs, and validate it against the current dirty tree.

tasks.title: Add autonomy handoff bundle verifier
tasks.summary: The handoff bundle can export tracked patches and untracked text content, but there is not yet a separate verifier that checks bundle schema, path safety, and content digests before another environment restores it. Add a read-only verifier for bundle JSON from stdin or file.
expectedFailureModes: A corrupted handoff bundle is accepted and another environment reconstructs the wrong files.
Unsafe absolute or traversal paths in bundle contents are accepted.
The verifier writes files or Git metadata while checking a bundle.
tasks.nextAction: Add an autonomy handoff bundle verifier with stdin/file input, verify patch and untracked-file digests plus path safety, document it in autonomous workflow docs, and validate it against a generated bundle.

tasks.title: Add autonomy handoff restore planner
tasks.summary: Handoff bundles can now be exported and verified, but a receiving environment still needs a deterministic, read-only plan for reconstructing tracked patches and untracked files safely. Add a restore planner that reads a verified bundle and emits ordered restore steps without writing files or Git metadata.
expectedFailureModes: A receiving environment applies bundle contents in an unsafe order and loses untracked file data.
The restore plan omits base commit or blocker context required to decide whether restoration is safe.
The restore planner writes files or Git metadata while only planning restoration.
tasks.nextAction: Add an autonomy handoff restore planner with stdin/file input and text/JSON output, document it in autonomous workflow docs, and validate it against a generated bundle.

tasks.title: Add autonomy handoff toolchain validator
tasks.summary: The handoff path now has separate dirty report, bundle export, verifier, and restore planner commands. Add one read-only validator that exercises the whole toolchain together so blocked sessions can prove the handoff artifacts are internally consistent.
expectedFailureModes: Individual handoff tools pass alone but fail when piped together.
The validator misses digest tampering and accepts a corrupt bundle.
The validator writes files, stages changes, commits, or pushes while checking handoff artifacts.
tasks.nextAction: Add a validate-autonomy-handoff command that runs the dirty report, bundle export, verifier, restore planner, and expected tamper rejection without writing Git metadata.

tasks.title: Add handoff validation to alpha readiness
tasks.summary: Alpha readiness now depends on commit-blocked sessions being able to export and verify complete handoff bundles, but the release readiness report does not yet check that handoff toolchain. Add the handoff validator as a read-only readiness signal and document the blocker semantics.
expectedFailureModes: Alpha readiness omits a broken handoff pipeline even though autonomous release preparation depends on dirty work being recoverable.
The readiness check accidentally writes Git metadata, stages files, commits, or pushes while exercising handoff validation.
Release docs list handoff validation as required but the machine-readable readiness report cannot expose that blocker.
tasks.nextAction: Wire validate-autonomy-handoff into alpha-release-readiness, document the readiness check in release docs, and validate the JSON/text paths without writing Git metadata.

tasks.title: Improve exhausted backlog guidance
tasks.summary: When the autonomy seed queue is exhausted, the command output still points operators at manual backlog editing instead of the validated scaffold workflow. Tighten the error text so autonomous sessions can refill the queue through the existing scaffold command.
expectedFailureModes: Autonomous sessions stall because the exhausted-backlog output omits the scaffold command.
Operators manually edit backlog templates and skip validator-friendly defaults already provided by the scaffold CLI.
The exhausted path exits with unclear instructions that do not name the validation and reseed sequence.
tasks.nextAction: Update autonomy-seed-next exhaustion output to reference the scaffold CLI and validation flow, then verify the exhausted path and autonomy records.

tasks.title: Add autonomy status gap report
tasks.summary: When the autonomy backlog is exhausted, agents need a durable source for the next alpha-critical task. Add a read-only report that extracts candidate hardening work from docs/status.md so backlog refills are grounded in the public capability matrix.
expectedFailureModes: Backlog refills depend on chat history instead of durable project status evidence.
The gap report misparses the status matrix and drops planned or experimental capabilities.
The gap report mutates files, stages changes, commits, or pushes while only selecting candidate work.
tasks.nextAction: Add an autonomy-status-gaps command that parses docs/status.md into text and JSON task candidates, document it in the autonomy workflow, and validate the report without mutating Git metadata.

tasks.title: Add autonomy review artifact scaffold
tasks.summary: The status gap report points at signed review artifacts for the autonomous workflow. Add the first truthful step: a read-only unsigned review artifact that binds a task record to its transition events and declared verification commands, without claiming cryptographic signing yet.
expectedFailureModes: Autonomous review evidence remains only in chat or event logs and cannot be exported as one task artifact.
Docs imply signed review artifacts exist before a signing policy or key custody path is implemented.
The artifact command writes files, stages changes, commits, or pushes while only summarizing task evidence.
tasks.nextAction: Add an autonomy-review-artifact command for task records, document the unsigned artifact boundary, update status evidence, and validate JSON/text output without writing Git metadata.

tasks.title: Add autonomy review artifact verifier
tasks.summary: Unsigned review artifacts now export task evidence, but there is no command that fails closed when a generated artifact drifts from the task record or event log. Add a read-only verifier that checks schema, safe source paths, task metadata, event selection, and digests before signing work begins.
expectedFailureModes: A review artifact with stale task metadata or event digests is accepted as evidence.
The verifier accepts absolute or traversal source paths from an artifact.
The verifier writes files, stages changes, commits, or pushes while only checking review evidence.
tasks.nextAction: Add an autonomy-verify-review-artifact command for JSON from stdin or file, document the verifier, update status evidence, and validate generated plus tampered artifact paths without writing Git metadata.

tasks.title: Add autonomy review artifact toolchain validator
tasks.summary: Review artifact generation and verification now exist as separate commands. Add one read-only validator that exercises generation, verification, and tamper rejection together so future signing work starts from a mechanically checked artifact pipeline.
expectedFailureModes: Review artifact generation and verification pass separately but fail when composed as the pipeline signing work would depend on.
The validator accepts tampered task or event digests and gives false confidence in review evidence.
The validator writes files, stages changes, commits, or pushes while checking a read-only review artifact pipeline.
tasks.nextAction: Add a validate-autonomy-review-artifacts command that generates an artifact, verifies it, rejects a tampered digest, document the command, update status evidence, and validate without writing Git metadata.

tasks.title: Add review artifact validation to alpha readiness
tasks.summary: The alpha readiness report checks handoff recovery but not the unsigned review artifact pipeline. Add the review artifact toolchain validator as a read-only alpha readiness signal so release preparation fails closed when task review evidence cannot be generated and verified.
expectedFailureModes: Alpha readiness omits a broken review artifact pipeline even though autonomous release evidence depends on task review artifacts.
The readiness check overclaims signed review artifacts instead of validating the unsigned artifact boundary.
The readiness check writes files, stages changes, commits, or pushes while exercising review artifact validation.
tasks.nextAction: Wire validate-autonomy-review-artifacts into alpha-release-readiness, update release docs/status, and validate JSON/text readiness output without writing Git metadata.

tasks.title: Add autonomy summary validator
tasks.summary: The autonomous workflow exposes a sprint summary generator, but there is no focused read-only check that its JSON and Markdown outputs remain machine-consumable. Add a validator so routine sprint-summary publication has a stable local gate.
expectedFailureModes: Sprint summaries render for humans but JSON output drifts and breaks machine consumers.
Summary limits or state totals become inconsistent, making published sprint evidence misleading.
The validator writes files, stages changes, commits, or pushes while only checking summary output.
tasks.nextAction: Add a validate-autonomy-summary command that checks Markdown output, JSON schema shape, count consistency, limit behavior, and invalid-argument rejection without writing Git metadata.

tasks.title: Gate alpha evidence on readiness state
tasks.summary: Alpha release evidence should carry the repository readiness report so draft bundles expose blockers and accepted bundles cannot ignore unresolved release gates.
expectedFailureModes: Accepted release bundles omit unresolved alpha readiness blockers.
Draft evidence cannot be generated from a dirty or commit-blocked checkout for handoff review.
Bundle validation accepts malformed readiness JSON or local machine identifiers.
humanEscalation: Human approval is still required before creating tags, publishing artifacts, or overriding release blockers.
tasks.nextAction: Embed alpha-release-readiness output in alpha release evidence, teach bundle validation to reject blocked accepted evidence, and document the draft override.

tasks.title: Version alpha release evidence schema
tasks.summary: Alpha release evidence should include a stable schema identifier so bundle validators and future release tooling can reject incompatible evidence instead of inferring shape from kind alone.
expectedFailureModes: Future release tooling accepts an unversioned evidence shape after the envelope changes.
Bundle validation relies on a loose kind field and misses incompatible evidence.
Docs describe evidence contents without naming the schema contract.
humanEscalation: Schema-breaking release evidence changes require human approval once published evidence exists.
tasks.nextAction: Add a schema field to alpha release evidence, require it in bundle validation, document the versioned envelope, and update the release evidence regression check.

tasks.title: Require explicit alpha gate outcomes
tasks.summary: Alpha release bundle validation should require every evidence command to carry an explicit outcome so accepted bundles cannot hide unrun gates by deleting the pending marker.
expectedFailureModes: Accepted release notes omit a gate result for a required evidence command.
Skipped gates are accepted without a reason.
Malformed gate result text bypasses acceptance validation.
humanEscalation: A release operator must still decide whether failed or skipped gates allow a rejected, superseded, or human-approved candidate decision.
tasks.nextAction: Parse validation.md required-gate lines, require result passed/failed/skipped for every evidence command, require skipped reasons, and document the result contract.

tasks.title: Bind accepted alpha decisions to passed gates
tasks.summary: Alpha bundle validation should reject an accepted decision when any required gate is failed, skipped, pending, or unchecked, even if draft or environment overrides are supplied.
expectedFailureModes: A bundle with decision accepted contains failed gates but still validates.
A bundle with decision accepted contains skipped gates but still validates.
Draft or environment overrides accidentally weaken the accepted-decision gate contract.
humanEscalation: A human release operator must decide whether failed or skipped gates justify rejected or superseded evidence instead of accepted evidence.
tasks.nextAction: Track parsed gate outcomes, require accepted decisions to have every evidence command passed, add regression coverage, and document the accepted-decision contract.

tasks.title: Add accepted alpha bundle fixture
tasks.summary: Alpha release evidence validation should prove the happy path too: a clean, ready, all-passed accepted bundle must validate without local environment overrides.
expectedFailureModes: The validator only proves rejection paths and misses a broken accepted-bundle path.
The synthetic fixture leaves temporary files under docs/releases.
The fixture relies on current dirty checkout state instead of a deterministic accepted evidence envelope.
humanEscalation: Published release schema changes still require human approval once real public bundles exist.
tasks.nextAction: Add a synthetic accepted bundle fixture to validate-alpha-release-evidence, document the positive acceptance coverage, and keep the fixture self-cleaning.

tasks.title: Scope alpha gate parsing to required gates
tasks.summary: Alpha bundle validation should only satisfy evidence commands from the Required Gates section so copied command lines elsewhere in validation.md cannot satisfy release acceptance.
expectedFailureModes: A command line outside Required Gates satisfies release acceptance.
Duplicate command lines inside and outside Required Gates produce ambiguous evidence.
Docs imply any matching command line in validation notes is enough.
humanEscalation: Published bundle format changes require human approval once real public release evidence exists.
tasks.nextAction: Parse the Required Gates section explicitly, validate gate result lines only from that section, add regression coverage, and document the section-scoped contract.

tasks.title: Scope alpha readiness blockers to readiness section
tasks.summary: Alpha bundle validation should only satisfy readiness blocker evidence from the Alpha Readiness section so copied blocker ids elsewhere in validation.md cannot satisfy blocker review.
expectedFailureModes: A readiness blocker copied outside Alpha Readiness satisfies bundle validation.
A bundle can omit blocker ids from the Alpha Readiness section but still validate.
Docs imply blocker ids anywhere in validation notes are enough.
humanEscalation: Published bundle format changes require human approval once real public release evidence exists.
tasks.nextAction: Parse the Alpha Readiness section explicitly, validate readiness blockers only from that section, add regression coverage, and document the section-scoped blocker contract.

tasks.title: Bind alpha validation notes to evidence metadata
tasks.summary: Alpha bundle validation should reject validation.md when its generated timestamp, candidate commit, branch, dirty count, readiness state, or status diverges from evidence.json.
expectedFailureModes: validation.md names a different candidate commit than evidence.json but still validates.
validation.md marks a blocked readiness report as ready but still validates.
validation.md status diverges from the recorded decision but still validates.
humanEscalation: Published bundle format changes require human approval once real public release evidence exists.
tasks.nextAction: Validate top-level validation.md metadata against evidence.json, add mismatch regression coverage, and document the metadata binding contract.

tasks.title: Add release bundle digest manifest
tasks.summary: Alpha release bundles currently bind evidence and validation notes, but they do not record stable file digests for bundle contents. Add a deterministic manifest so operators can verify bundle files have not drifted before signatures or public transparency are implemented.
expectedFailureModes: A release bundle file changes after review without any local integrity signal.
The manifest records nondeterministic metadata that changes on every validation run.
Docs imply signed or public transparency guarantees when the implementation only provides local digest binding.
tasks.nextAction: Generate manifest.json with SHA-256 digests for evidence.json and validation.md, validate the manifest in the bundle gate, document the contract, and add regression coverage for tampered bundle files.

tasks.title: Require release manifest file inventory
tasks.summary: The alpha release bundle manifest now records digests for scaffolded files, but the validator should also reject extra bundle files that are not listed in the manifest. Require the manifest inventory to match the bundle's regular files so future provenance or artifact files cannot be added without digest coverage.
expectedFailureModes: A release bundle gains an extra file after review without any manifest digest.
Recursive bundle files are skipped because only top-level scaffold files are inventoried.
The validator accepts unsafe or non-portable manifest paths while checking inventory coverage.
tasks.nextAction: Teach the bundle validator to compare manifest entries with the bundle file inventory, generate recursive relative paths, document the exact coverage rule, and add regression coverage for an unmanifested file.

tasks.title: Add scripts-only validation gate
tasks.summary: Add a validate.sh mode that runs autonomy, provenance, docs, and repository guardrails without requiring a Rust toolchain.
expectedFailureModes: Contributors in constrained environments cannot run any validation because Rust builds are mandatory.
Scripts-only validation accidentally invokes cargo and fails when Rust tooling is unavailable.
Docs imply script-only validation is equivalent to the full integration gate.
tasks.nextAction: Extend agent-os/scripts/validate.sh with a --scripts mode and document the new gate.

tasks.title: Treat MCP transport EOF as closed
tasks.summary: MCP subprocess servers can exit or EOF unexpectedly. Normalize stdio EOF to a first-class transport closed error so callers can handle crashes and shutdowns predictably.
expectedFailureModes: Tool bootstrap hangs or returns opaque errors when the MCP server exits after initialize.
EOF on stdout is reported as a JSON-RPC error instead of McpClientError::Closed, making error handling inconsistent.
Docs/tests claim in-flight requests resolve with Closed but actual behavior diverges.
tasks.nextAction: Map subprocess EOF to McpClientError::Closed and cover it with fake-server stdio tests.

tasks.title: Accept string JSON-RPC ids in MCP transport
tasks.summary: Some MCP servers respond with numeric JSON-RPC ids encoded as strings. Accept numeric strings while rejecting non-numeric ids so responses do not hang or route incorrectly.
expectedFailureModes: Response ids like "1" fail JSON parsing and leave requests hanging.
Non-numeric string ids are treated as matching and route responses to the wrong request.
Fake server cannot simulate string-id responses for live coverage.
tasks.nextAction: Teach covenant-mcp transport to parse numeric-string response ids and cover it with unit plus fake-server tests.
